 Order

The instant miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act has been filed by the appellant-claimant being aggrieved by the impugned Award dated 05.04.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Vidisha in Claim Case No. 113 of 2016, seeking enhancement of the compensation amount and also challenging the finding whereby the Claims Tribunal has exonerated the Insurance Company from its liability to pay compensation.
2. Along with the appeal, the appellant has filed I.A. No. 3389 of 2019, an application for condonation of delay in filing the appeal.
3. As per the office report, there is a delay of 19 days in filing the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11374 2 MA-4503-2019 4.
Considering the reasons assigned in the application, which are duly supported by an affidavit, the same is allowed.
The delay in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.
5. The date of accident and the factum of negligence are not in dispute.

1 6.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in holding that the owner and driver of the offending vehicle breached the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is further submitted that the Insurance Company did not adduce any cogent evidence to establish that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the relevant time.
In absence of such evidence, the finding of breach recorded by the Claims Tribunal is unsustainable in law.
It is also contended that the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is on the lower side and deserves enhancement.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has supported the impugned Award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned Award as well as the record of the Claims Tribunal.
9.
It is a settled principle of law that the burden to prove breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy lies upon the Insurance Company.
Unless such breach is established by leading cogent and reliable evidence, the Insurance Company cannot be exonerated from its liability.

10. Upon perusal of the record, it is found that the Insurance Company has failed to produce any satisfactory evidence to prove that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence.
In NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11374 3 MA-4503-2019 absence of such proof, the finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal exonerating the Insurance Company is erroneous and cannot be sustained.
The same is hereby set aside.

11. Accordingly, it is held that the Insurance Company shall be liable to pay the compensation amount to the claimant, jointly and severally with the owner and driver of the offending vehicle,
with the primary liability to satisfy the Award being that of the Insurance Company.

12. So far as enhancement of compensation is concerned, considering the nature of injuries sustained by the appellant-claimant, this Court finds it appropriate to award an additional sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) over and above the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The aforesaid enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.
The enhanced amount shall be paid by the Insurance Company within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
13. With the aforesaid modification in the impugned Award, the appeal stands partly allowed and is accordingly disposed of.
14. CC as per rules.
